note: AHA pages (cpr.heart.org, professional.heart.org) returned 403 to WebFetch and curl; NCBI Bookshelf returned a captcha. Used OpenStax, MedlinePlus, Cleveland Clinic, AHA newsroom, PMC and others instead.

questions.note: Answer matches AHA hands-only approach for untrained bystanders.

claims.claim: Homeostatic loop = sensor, control center comparing to set point, effector; negative feedback opposes the change
Labor: cervical stretch triggers oxytocin release which strengthens contractions (positive feedback); clotting also positive feedback
In fever the hypothalamic set point is raised, so the person feels cold and shivers until reaching the new temperature
Left ventricle wall is much thicker than the right because it pumps through the systemic circuit; four valves tricuspid, mitral, pulmonary, aortic
Sinoatrial node is the natural pacemaker; impulse passes through AV node; ECG records this activity
Cardiac output = heart rate x stroke volume, roughly 5 L/min at rest in an adult
claims.note: Cleveland Clinic gives 5-6 L/min at rest.

claims.claim: Inspiration: diaphragm contracts and flattens, intra-alveolar pressure falls below atmospheric; brainstem drives breathing mainly by CO2/pH rather than oxygen
ADH makes the collecting duct reabsorb more water; aldosterone makes it retain sodium
Lungs adjust CO2 within minutes, kidneys adjust bicarbonate/acid over hours to days; faster breathing lowers CO2 and makes blood less acidic
claims.note: 'About a million nephrons' per kidney not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Thyroid hormone feeds back to lower TSH; low thyroid hormone raises TSH
In hypothyroidism from gland failure TSH is high while thyroid hormone is low
Adrenaline released rapidly from adrenal medulla via sympathetic system; cortisol from adrenal cortex acts over longer periods
Necrosis provokes inflammation; apoptosis is programmed, tidy cell death
Histamine dilates vessels (redness, heat) and increases permeability (swelling); neutrophils arrive first, macrophages later
Heart muscle heals mainly with collagen scar, while skin surface and liver regenerate; NSAIDs act by blocking prostaglandin synthesis
Antibiotics do nothing against viruses such as colds, and every antibiotic use adds side effects and resistance risk
A newborn carries antibodies from the mother that give temporary protection
claims.note: CDC: passive maternal immunity fades within weeks or months.

claims.claim: Vaccines create memory so later exposure triggers a faster, stronger secondary response
claims.note: CDC page describes residual 'watch' white cells rather than using the term memory cells; consistent.

claims.claim: TP53 is a tumor suppressor that halts damaged cells or triggers their death
Human papillomavirus causes cervical cancer; screening by cytology or HPV testing
claims.note: NCI: virtually all cervical cancer is caused by HPV.

claims.claim: Metastasis is spread through blood or lymph to distant organs and is the main reason cancer kills
claims.note: NCI page confirms spread via blood/lymph; the 'main reason cancer kills' part was not stated on the opened page.

claims.claim: Cystic fibrosis is autosomal recessive, caused by CFTR variants; CFTR encodes a chloride channel; thick mucus in lungs and pancreas
Sickle cell: one amino acid change in beta-globin; sickled cells block vessels (pain) and break down early (anemia)
claims.note: Malaria-protection statement not checked on an opened page.

claims.claim: Hemophilia A is X-linked recessive; males more often affected because they have one X chromosome
Diabetes diagnostic thresholds: fasting plasma glucose >=126 mg/dL or A1c >=6.5%, confirmation needed without clear symptoms
claims.note: ADA current.

claims.claim: A1c reflects average glucose over roughly the past two to three months
Without insulin the body burns fat producing ketones; DKA is an emergency with nausea, rapid deep breathing, abdominal pain
In the United States, the 2017 ACC/AHA guideline defines hypertension as 130/80 mm Hg or higher
claims.note: Stale citation: the current US guideline is the 2025 AHA/ACC multisociety High Blood Pressure guideline (Aug 2025), which keeps the 2017 categories and the >=130/80 threshold. Text should cite the 2025 guideline; the number itself is still correct.

claims.claim: Plaque rupture leads to rapid clot formation that blocks the coronary artery, causing myocardial infarction
Statins such as atorvastatin inhibit HMG-CoA reductase and reduce heart attack risk
claims.note: FDA Lipitor label: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor indicated to reduce risk of MI and stroke.

claims.claim: Current international guidance emphasizes that relying on a reliever alone is not enough for persistent asthma (albuterol framed as the reliever)
claims.note: Out of date/understated: GINA 2025 says SABA-only treatment is not recommended at any step (adults/adolescents), not just persistent asthma, and the preferred reliever is as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol, so 'reliever alone' with ICS-formoterol is actually a recommended mild-asthma option. Lesson should say SABA-only rather than reliever-only.

claims.claim: Albuterol is a bronchodilator that relaxes and opens the airways within minutes
claims.note: MedlinePlus confirms bronchodilator action; beta-2 mechanism not explicitly stated there.

claims.claim: COPD is mainly caused by smoking
Swallowed drugs pass via the portal vein to the liver and undergo first-pass metabolism; IV drugs avoid this
claims.note: Secondary educational source.

claims.claim: A drug that inhibits a liver (CYP) enzyme raises levels of drugs it clears; an inducer lowers them
Warfarin needs careful monitoring because small changes matter; bleeding is a predictable adverse effect; interactions with supplements
claims.note: MedlinePlus: regular INR testing, serious bleeding risk, many interactions.

claims.claim: Typical resting adult values: heart rate 60-100, respiratory rate about 12-20, oral temperature about 36.5-37.5 C
claims.note: HR matches exactly. MedlinePlus and Cleveland Clinic give RR 12-18 and temp 36.5-37.3 C; lesson's 12-20 and 37.5 are commonly used approximations, labelled approximate. SpO2 >=95% not checked.

claims.claim: Troponin, a protein in heart muscle cells, rises in blood when they are damaged and is central to diagnosing heart attack
Creatinine is a muscle waste product cleared by the kidneys; a rise suggests reduced kidney filtration
MRI uses magnetic fields and radio waves, no ionizing radiation; metal implants/devices require screening
CT uses ionizing radiation; medical imaging radiation adds a small lifetime cancer risk; ordered when benefit justifies it
Ultrasound is radiation-free, standard for fetal imaging, and struggles with air and bone
Herd immunity threshold is roughly 1 - 1/R0; measles R0 often cited ~12 (12-18), needing ~92% or more
claims.note: Source uses R0 15 giving ~93%, target 95%; lesson's R0 12 -> 92% is the low end of the commonly cited 12-18 range.

claims.claim: Measles is extremely contagious
claims.note: CDC: up to 9 of 10 susceptible close contacts infected.

claims.claim: Incidence = new cases over a period; prevalence = existing cases at a point in time
claims.note: Standard definition; not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Number needed to treat = 1 / absolute risk reduction; 2% -> 1% is 50% RRR, 1-point ARR, NNT about 100
Statistical significance is not the same as importance; a tiny effect can be significant in a huge trial
claims.note: ASA 2016 principle 5.

claims.claim: Randomization spreads known and unknown confounders by chance; meta-analysis usually tops the evidence hierarchy
claims.note: Standard teaching; not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Beauchamp and Childress set out four principles: autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, justice
Valid consent needs capacity and information on nature, risks, benefits and alternatives; emergency exception when patient cannot decide
claims.note: AMA Code of Medical Ethics 2.1.1.

claims.claim: HIPAA privacy rules limit sharing of health information, with permitted disclosures such as required public health reporting
Adult compressions at 100-120/min, depth about 5-6 cm (2-2.4 in), full recoil; trained rescuers 30:2
claims.note: UC Davis guide based on 2025 AHA guidelines: at least 2 in, not over 2.4 in, 100-120/min, 30:2. Unchanged in the Oct 2025 AHA update.

claims.claim: Current first-aid guidance for choking adults includes back blows and abdominal thrusts
claims.note: 2025 AHA guidelines (22 Oct 2025) newly recommend alternating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts for conscious adults; lesson is current.

claims.claim: For each minute of delay in defibrillation the chance of survival drops substantially
claims.note: About 7-10% per minute without CPR.

claims.claim: Severe bleeding: firm direct pressure; tourniquet for life-threatening limb bleeding
Face drooping, arm weakness and speech trouble suggest stroke; call emergency services immediately
Physician path: bachelor's degree, 4-year medical school (MD or DO, DO adds musculoskeletal emphasis), residency (~3 years primary care, longer for others), state licensure
claims.note: BLS: 4 years medical school, 3-9 years residency, all states require licensure.

claims.claim: Nurse practitioners hold a graduate degree; scope of practice set by each state
Physician assistants complete a master's-level program; pharmacists hold a Doctor of Pharmacy
Supplements in the United States are not required to prove effectiveness before sale
claims.note: FDA lacks authority to approve supplements before marketing.

claims.claim: A relative change such as doubling a very small risk can sound large while the absolute change is tiny
No good evidence shows juice cleanses/detoxes add benefit; liver and kidneys clear waste
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page.
